I1.evidence: The code uses formal, structured representations: the OxCal model is written in OxCal's CQL2 modelling grammar ('comprises two sections; the first defines the likelihoods and their constraints, and the second defines occurrences for each of the bead types', p.11), and the figure-reproduction code is R using the ArchaeoPhases package's functions -- both machine-parseable languages, not prose or images.

I2.evidence: No evidence of FAIR-compliant controlled-vocabulary usage in the code itself.

I3.evidence: The code's key dependency is cited with a qualified, DOI-bearing reference: 'The modes of change can be investigated with the joint posteriors recorded in the MCMC output of a Bayesian model using functions provided by ArchaeoPhases software (Philippe & Vibet, 2020)' (p.23), full citation 'Philippe, A., & Vibet, M.-A. (2020). Analysis of archaeological phases using the CRAN package ArchaeoPhases. Journal of Statistical Software, 93. https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v093.c01' (references, p.28) -- a typed ('uses software X') reference anchored to a resolvable DOI, standing in for the code's own metadata (none exists independently per Row 6). Note: the evidence pack's own attempt to resolve the ArchaeoPhases CRAN record directly returned no usable fields (record cran:https://cran.r-project.org/package=ArchaeoPhases, status 'endpoint-flagged', a recorded gap per erratum-log Entry 3 item 8) -- the I3 credit rests on the paper's own DOI citation of the companion JSS article, not on the CRAN record.

R1.evidence: The Supplement's code content is described with specific structure and detail: 'It comprises two sections; the first defines the likelihoods and their constraints, and the second defines occurrences for each of the bead types' (p.11); the ArchaeoPhases-based plotting code is documented via its companion JSS software paper (Philippe & Vibet, 2020) and its authorship/maintenance attributed in the paper's contributions statement ('AP maintains the ArchaeoPhases software, improved the R code for tempo and occurrence plots, and augmented their description in the text', p.24).

R1_1.evidence: No licence is separately stated for the Supplement anywhere in the paper, so the v2.1 default applies: 'absent a separate supplement licence, default to same-as-paper.' The paper's cover sheet states 'Article available under the terms of the CC-BY-NC-ND licence (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/)' and 'This article is distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs (CC BY-NC-ND) licence' (p.1) -- a clear, accessible, specifically identified licence (its NC-ND restrictiveness notwithstanding; R1.1 tests clarity, not openness). Caveat for the record: the evidence-pack Crossref record for the article carries only Elsevier text-and-data-mining policy links, not an explicit CC grant (record crossref:10.1016/j.jas.2023.105765) -- reflecting the Version-of-Record's publisher-side registration; this is not treated as an explicitly stated, conflicting reuse licence for the same artefact (TDM policies are not themselves a reuse-licence assertion), so no most-restrictive override is applied. Code has a single principal artefact (the Supplement), so unlike data_fair.R1_1 this call is not diluted by conjunctive scoring against a second artefact.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance documented: software and calibration-curve versions ('OxCal version 4.4.2 and the IntCal20 calibration curve (Reimer et al., 2020)', p.11), replication checks ('five independent runs of the model indicate negligible between-run variability', p.11), and an explicit account of which constraints from the prior Bayliss et al. (2013) model were retained or removed and why (pp.10-11).

R1_3.evidence: The Supplement does not qualify under any listed R1.3 route: not deposited in an accredited domain repository (Row 6, no accreditation), and the paper's own OxCal/R scripts show no package structure, CITATION.cff, or CodeMeta. The third-party ArchaeoPhases dependency is itself a reviewed CRAN package with a JSS publication, but per the v2.1 aggregation rule that status does not transfer to the principal code artefact ('third-party dependencies are never substitutes for [the paper's own scripts]...enter scoring only through citation quality (I3) and the evidence pack').

I1.evidence: Both principal artefacts use structured, formal representations. The Supplement's data content is embedded in the OxCal model, 'comprises two sections; the first defines the likelihoods and their constraints, and the second defines occurrences for each of the bead types' (p.11) -- OxCal's CQL2 is a formal, machine-parseable modelling grammar, not free text or images.

I2.evidence: No evidence of a FAIR-compliant controlled vocabulary (e.g. PeriodO, Getty AAT, Darwin Core) applied to either principal artefact. Bead-type codes used throughout (e.g. 'BE1-Amethyst', 'BE1-CylPen', 'BE2-c', 'BE3-Amber'; figs. 3-6) read as a project/typology-specific coding scheme (Brugmann, 2004; Nielsen, 2013) with no cited external vocabulary PID.

I3.evidence: No qualified references (typed links to other resources via PIDs) evidenced for either principal data artefact. The evidence-pack DataCite record for the ADS deposit (datacite:10.5284/1018290) does not surface a relatedIdentifiers field, and no platform-table entitlement grants this by construction for DataCite or Row 6. Ladder exhausted without a positive signal.

R1.evidence: Both principal artefacts are richly described. ADS deposit sits within a well-documented project: 'well documented, with a detailed description of the chronological analysis (see Baxter, 2014), a relational database deposited with the Archaeological Data Service that catalogs the graves and finds (Hines, 2013), a hierarchical Bayesian chronological model constructed by an experienced chronologist (Bayliss et al., 2013), and bead identifications by an expert (Nielsen, 2013)' (p.10). The Supplement's data content is described with specific structure and versioning: 'It comprises two sections...The revised model calibrates with OxCal version 4.4.2 and the IntCal20 calibration curve (Reimer et al., 2020)' (p.11).

R1_1.evidence: Conjunctive failure. The ADS deposit's licence is recorded in the evidence pack only as 'ADS Terms and Conditions apply to reuse' (record datacite:10.5284/1018290) -- a generic pointer, not a specific identifiable licence (no CC/ODbL/SPDX code); per R1.1 rule (b), 'where the paper is silent [it is], artefacts on third-party services are scored on the licence recorded at the service... a platform's mandatory licence field does not itself satisfy R1.1; the licence must be identified.' The Supplement component alone would score 1 via the 'same-as-paper' default (no separate supplement licence stated; paper's cover sheet: 'Article available under the terms of the CC-BY-NC-ND licence (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/)', p.1). Because R1.1 is scored conjunctively across every principal dataset, the ADS component's ambiguous licence brings the overall data R1.1 to 0.

R1_2.evidence: Both principal artefacts show detailed provenance. ADS deposit sits within an extensively documented dating project (Hines & Bayliss, 2013; Baxter, 2014 commentary). The Supplement documents specific processing/versioning provenance: software and calibration-curve versions ('OxCal version 4.4.2 and the IntCal20 calibration curve (Reimer et al., 2020)', p.11), replication checks ('five independent runs of the model indicate negligible between-run variability', p.11), and an explicit account of which original Bayliss et al. (2013) constraints were retained versus removed, with reasons given (pp.10-11).

R1_3.evidence: Conjunctive failure. ADS component alone scores 1 by construction: platform-table Row 4 states 'ADS (Archaeology Data Service): mandatory validated core template plus category-specific technical metadata, enforced at ingest -- an ingest-enforced domain metadata standard; R1.3 = 1 by construction', matching the evidence-pack's confirmed publisher 'Archaeology Data Service' (record datacite:10.5284/1018290). The Supplement component does not qualify under any listed R1.3 route: not deposited in an accredited domain repository (Row 6, no accreditation), and no generic/domain metadata schema conformance is demonstrated for the OxCal model/data content itself. Conjunctive result: 0.
